newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: U.S. envoy in shuttle to avert Kinshasa bloodbath.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy in shuttle to avert Kinshasa bloodbath.

text.p: U.S. envoy Bill Richardson met two key African leaders on Tuesday in his continuing bid to prevent a bloodbath as Zairean rebels close in on the capital Kinshasa.
Richardson met Ugandan leader Yoweri Museveni and Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe at a lodge in the Botswana border town of Kasane.

He was due to fly to Cape Town later in the day to see South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who is also playing a central role in diplomatic efforts to engineer a peaceful end to the Zaire crisis.

Uganda is a key supporter of Laurent Kabila's rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire. Rebel forces are now said to be only a day or two away from entering Zaire's capital, practically the last bastion of President Mobutu Sese Seko.
Asked if he would give the command to evacuate Americans and other foreign nationals from Kinshasa, the envoy said: "That would have to be authorised by the State Department."
He said the U.S. ambassador in Kinshasa, Dan Simpson, had been fully briefed.

Speaking in Lubumbashi on Monday after meeting rebel leader Laurent Kabila, Richardson said: "The objective of my urgent mission is to prepare a soft landing for Mr Kabila's rebels when they reach Kinshasa, a landing that avoids bloodshed and chaos."

Troops from the United States, Belgium, France and Britain are on standby in Brazzaville, the Congo capital just across the river from Kinshasa, ready to airlift foreigners to safety if a battle for Zaire's biggest city of five million people becomes inevitable.
